messages:
olivia: Quick design review — the approval modal + scorecard density feels like it downplays the 'why' for an approve. When we compress rows the affordance to explain a decision disappears. Need thoughts on microcopy and visual weight. :thinking_face:
samir: Agreed. In compact mode the 'confidence' chip is the only signifier and it's ambiguous. People read it as model confidence not reviewer confidence.
mia: +1. Also screen reader flow: when you approve we should announce the selected reason or a short summary, otherwise it's just "approved" and you lose context.
jordan: Can we try separating two axes: a small compact badge for model score + a short human-reason line that toggles visible in compact mode? Example mock:```Model: GPT-4o · ModelScore: 87% · Reviewer: Mia — "prefers shorter output for UI"```But inline that feels noisy.
olivia: Proposal for microcopy options (short form for compact rows):
- Badge label: "Model §87" (where § is subtle icon)
- Reviewer short: "Reason: brevity" (truncated, hover to expand)
- Full modal copy: "Approve this regression? Your approval records a reviewer note and the selected scorecard reason."
samir: For the approve CTA we should avoid ambiguous verbs. Suggest: `Confirm approval` vs `Approve and publish` vs `Approve (private)` depending on rollout. Also add a subtle secondary: `Add note` inline so accidental approves are less likely.
mia: Love the `Confirm approval` idea. Also keyboard: when focus lands on CTA, pressing Enter should open a small inline note textarea rather than immediately submit. Low friction but prevents accidental confirms.
jordan: UX bot mock of modal content:```Title: Confirm approval of selected diffsCopy: You're approving 12 items. This action will mark them as accepted in the scorecard and may affect downstream alerts.Reviewer note (optional): [textarea]Checkbox: Notify team on approve [ ]Primary CTA: Confirm approvalSecondary CTA: Cancel```
a11y-bot: Accessibility nits:
- Ensure primary CTA has aria-describedby linking to the reviewer-note label so screen readers can announce optionality.
- Announce with polite live region: `Approval confirmed: 12 items. Reviewer note: {first 120 chars}`.
- Focus management: return focus to the diff list item that was nearest the viewport so keyboard users retain context.
olivia: UX copy variants to A/B:
A) Short: `Confirm approval` / `Add an optional note`
B) Explicit: `Approve and record reviewer note` / `Skip note`
C) Progressive: `Confirm approval` + appear inline note only if user hits arrow key or types (less visual noise)
samir: I'd run A/B with keyboard-first users to measure accidental approve rate and time-to-approve. Metric: approvals with empty note % and accidental undo rate within 60s.
mia: Another small visual tweak: give the reviewer-reason a 600 weight vs model-confidence 400 so human intent reads stronger in compressed rows. Contrast tweak only.
jordan: One more thought on compact diff: add a micro affordance `•` that opens a stacked context drawer rather than expanding inline — keeps density but allows fast access.
olivia: Action items: 1) design to produce two mock variants (A short + C progressive) 2) copy team to draft 3 microcopy strings for CTAs 3) eng to prototype keyboard behavior (Enter opens note) 4) a11y to draft announcement phrasing. I'll track in the PRD.
samir: I pushed an initial prototype figma link: https://fig.ma/abc123 — highlights in the comments.
mia: I'll write the a11y phrasing sample: `Approval confirmed for {n} items. Reviewer note: {summary}` and post it in the PRD.
jordan: :thumbsup: happy with this. Small follow-up: if we show reviewer name, display initials only in compact and full name in modal.
olivia: Great — thanks everyone. I'll drop the mock variants and copy doc by EOD and tag you. :sparkles:
